title: The Stag Hunt
subtitle: Lose twice. Learn why. The only honest game in the plaza.

customObject.name: the game table
customObject.description: a small round table with two carved tokens — a stag and a hare — and a floating scoreboard that keeps embarrassing everyone

script.note: The plaza, evening. A brass-coloured robot stands behind a small table. Two carved tokens: a stag, a hare. A sign reads: LOSE TWICE. LEARN WHY.

script.text: Step up, step up. Two players, two buttons, one tragedy. I am Axiom, and I run the only honest game in this plaza.

And yet here you are. The rules: you each choose in secret — share, or take. Both share: three points each. Both take: one point each. You take while she shares: five for you, nothing for her. Choose.

script.note: They press. The scoreboard lights up: TAKE. TAKE. One point each.

script.text: I felt bad, and did it anyway.

Of course you did — you played correctly! Against a stranger you will never see again, taking wins no matter what she does. Two intelligent people, reasoning perfectly, walking hand in hand into the worst outcome. It has a name: the prisoner's dilemma. And it is not a puzzle about evil people. It is a puzzle about a badly built game.
So people defect because the game is shaped wrong. Not because they're rotten.
Hold that thought — round two. Same rules, one change: you play each other again tomorrow. And the day after. No announced ending. And you both remember.

script.note: They press. SHARE. SHARE. Again. Again. The two scores climb together.

script.text: Because the future casts a shadow. Last century they ran tournaments of strategies against each other, and the winner was embarrassingly simple: start friendly, do what was done to you, forgive quickly. Nice strategies beat clever ones — but only when the game repeats. Cooperation is not a virtue, my friends. It is an equilibrium. You just have to live somewhere that lets you reach it.

The older, deeper game. A stag feeds a village but takes every hunter to bring down. A hare feeds one, and you can snare it alone. Hunt the stag and your partner doesn't show — you starve. So among strangers, everyone quietly hunts hare. Small lives, guaranteed. And the stag — the school, the garden, the workshop, the whole better place — stays in the forest. Not because anyone is wicked. Because no one can be sure the others will come.
So how does anyone ever get the stag?

You need to know your partners will be there tomorrow. Which means: partners you chose. Games that repeat. Reputation that is visible. And doors that open outward — an honest exit keeps everyone honest. Change those four things, and the same people, same brains, same flaws, start hunting stag. You cannot sermon a town into trust. You can build a town where trust is the winning move.
One more. Say we're meant to meet somewhere in this city — no time agreed, no place agreed. Where do you go?

Obviously! Nobody told you, and everybody knows. A meeting point no one chose and everyone chose — the mathematicians call it a focal point. A community is one enormous agreement of exactly that kind: a place where everyone knows that everyone will come. Now. Again? Double or nothing on the hare.
So this community isn't asking people to be better than they are.
It is letting them stop pretending to be worse. Table's open till late.

script.note: The stag token catches the lamplight. On the scoreboard, both numbers are still climbing.
